name: Major cyber incidents
value: France blames IRGC unit for store sabotage
summary: France blamed an IRGC-linked unit on 9–10 Nov for October hacks on about 700 sites' fridges that caused 15 fires
state: France's foreign ministry attributed the 11–12 Oct attacks on refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites to Shahid Kaveh, a unit tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guards; authorities cite at least 15 fires and tens of millions of euros in losses (BleepingComputer, 9 Nov). Iran called the accusations baseless on 10 Nov (Al Jazeera). The later 2 Nov wave in several European countries has not been attributed. A destructive state-attributed attack keeps the Alert.
for_you: Organisations running building or refrigeration control systems can follow NCSC guidance on securing internet-exposed operational technology. Shoppers are not directly exposed beyond possible local stock shortages.
rubric_hit: Destructive state-attributed attack: France attributes Oct sabotage of ~700 sites to IRGC-linked unit (9–10 Nov)

sources.title: BleepingComputer — France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
